name: Fitness API Changes & Deadlines 2026
methodology: One row per dated ecosystem event tracked on https://aifitnessapi.com/changes — deprecations, deadlines, term changes, model freezes. The status field is the point of the dataset: confirmed means a vendor's own words are quoted on the linked page; reported means vendor or community notices we could not confirm on an official page; watch means an undated live risk. Date precision is kept exactly as sourced ("2026-09" means a reported month) and is never sharpened. Every row links the page on this site that carries the sourced claim, and verifiedOn records when that page was last checked. The undated watch items published on /changes are excluded here because they carry no date to publish.

fields.date: Event date at the precision the source supports (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD)
fields.sortDate: Full ISO date used only for ordering when `date` is fuzzy
fields.title: Short name of the event
fields.summary: What changed, in the words the linked page can support
fields.status: confirmed | reported | watch — the evidence grade, see methodology
fields.source: aifitnessapi.com page carrying the sourced claim
fields.verifiedOn: Date this entry was last checked against its source page

items.title: Google Fit APIs: end of documented support
items.summary: Google's Fit migration guide on developer.android.com (updated September 10, 2026) states "The Google Fit APIs will be supported until the end of 2026" — end of support, with no switch-off date published. It recommends the Google Health API for cloud-based integrations (including the Fit History and Session APIs), Health Connect for step tracking and mobile-first apps, and Health Services on Wear OS, and lists no replacement for the Goals API.

items.title: Terra legacy widget endpoint deprecation
items.summary: Terra relaunched its connect widget. Its documentation says the older session endpoint, POST https://api.tryterra.co/v2/auth/generateWidgetSession, "keeps working today, with deprecation planned for 3 November 2026", and that "Accounts created after 3 September 2026 cannot use it at all." New sessions are created at POST https://access.tryterra.co/api/widget/session; the response shape (session_id, url, status, expires_in) is unchanged, while the multi-provider and all-providers options are now sent differently.

items.title: Fitbit Web API turn-off
items.summary: Google's Google Health API page states that on October 30, 2026 "the Fitbit Web API will be turned off and will no longer function or sync data to or from Fitbit users", and that all current integrations "must migrate their applications and users to the Google Health API and Google OAuth 2.0 as soon as possible". Until then the legacy API keeps operating without support, and Google's migration guide has apps support both login methods while it does. Existing tokens cannot be transferred, so every user re-consents through Google OAuth.

items.title: Open Wearables adds a paid Pro plan and ships outbound webhooks
items.summary: Open Wearables gives no date for the change: first seen on 2026-10-27, absent from its pages on 2026-10-17. Its pricing page now lists three plans: Core, self-hosted at "$0 Forever" under the MIT licence; Pro, "From $999 a month, per deployment", with health scores and other licensed modules; and Enterprise, a custom-priced annual agreement that carries the BAA. Its FAQ now says "Health scores come with Pro" and "Pro is priced per deployment rather than per user". Outbound webhooks, which its FAQ and webhooks page called in development on 2026-10-17, are now described as shipped: signed, retried and off by default.

items.title: Garmin Connect Personal API and Starter/Enterprise access
items.summary: Garmin reorganised its Connect Developer Program and gives no launch date: first seen on 2026-10-22, absent from the 2026-10-17 snapshot. A new Garmin Connect Personal API lets individuals create their own API key on Garmin Connect Web for their own data; Garmin says it "is available for personal use" and "is not intended for commercial applications serving multiple end users". The business program now describes Starter Access and Enterprise Access, its FAQ moved under a new Business section (the old address no longer loads), and the earlier FAQ statement that the program was only for business use is gone.

items.title: Sahha replaces its Free plan with a 30-day free trial
items.summary: Sahha's pricing page no longer lists a Free plan. The Internet Archive's capture of 2026-10-17 shows Free at $0 for 30 days, to "Build and test in sandbox" with 25 development users; on 2026-10-22 the page instead offers "Try any plan for 30 days", with "Card required, nothing charged today" and "Cancel before it ends and pay nothing". Starter ($299 a month billed annually, 1,000 users) and Pro ($1,499, 10,000 users) are unchanged. Sahha gives no date for the change, and its homepage FAQ still says to "Start free with 25 development users" in sandbox.

items.title: Fitbit Web API end of support
items.summary: Google's Google Health API page states that on September 30, 2026 "support for the Fitbit Web API ends. The API will continue to operate, but Google will no longer fix bugs or provide API support." The turn-off follows on October 30, 2026. Third-party guides had named September 30 before Google published the timeline; it is the end-of-support date, not the switch-off.

items.title: This site served HTTP 402 for five days
items.summary: From 2026-09-27 (21:38 UTC, the first probe that saw it) until recovery on 2026-10-02, every request to aifitnessapi.com answered HTTP 402 with x-vercel-error: DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED — Vercel had disabled the project's deployments, which is an account and billing state, not a code, build or DNS fault. Googlebot and bingbot got that status on every URL for five days, and a sustained 4xx reads as removal rather than retry. The site serves 200 again on the apex and on www. This entry is about this site rather than a vendor API, and it is here because a tracker that goes dark for five days and does not say so is not a record.

items.title: FTC rescinds its 2021 health-app breach policy statement
items.summary: The FTC's press release says "The Federal Trade Commission rescinded the 2021 Policy Statement on Breaches by Health Apps and Other Connected Devices", because the Commission's 2024 update to the Health Breach Notification Rule covers "health apps and connected devices like fitness trackers, rendering the policy statement unnecessary." The FTC's rule page dates the release September 9, 2026. The rule itself, 16 CFR part 318, still applies; eCFR's current text lists no amendment after May 30, 2024.
items.sourceLabel: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule for fitness apps

items.title: Strava developer terms: Standard Tier subscription
items.summary: Strava's API Policy makes Standard Tier apps "subject to subscription requirements", including "that the developer or specified end users maintain an active Strava subscription", and its getting-started guide calls a subscription "a prerequisite for creating an app". Access itself is free: the API Agreement (2026), effective June 1, 2026, says it is "currently provided at no charge". The architectural constraints matter more than the fee: Strava data may be shown only to the athlete it belongs to, and the API Policy forbids using it in the development, training, evaluation or operation of any AI application. Graded reported until Strava's own pages were re-read on 2026-10-17.

items.title: Fitbit accounts: Google Account consolidation gate (reported)
items.summary: Users on legacy Fitbit-only logins are reported to need consolidation into a Google Account by roughly mid-May 2026. Google's migration guide confirms the gate itself but gives no date: a user must sign in to the Google Health mobile app to link Google Health to their Google Account before an app can sync their data, and calls made before that fail with ACCOUNT_NOT_LINKED. A gate on your migration, not a detail inside it.

items.title: WHOOP membership restructuring
items.summary: Reported, not confirmed: 2026 press coverage said WHOOP had restructured its membership and upgrade model, and this site's WHOOP pricing page repeated it until the page was re-verified on 2026-10-17. WHOOP's developer pages read for that re-verification do not mention a restructuring. They do say a developer must have a WHOOP membership to build an app and that users connect with their own WHOOP accounts, so a membership change moves two columns of the cost model at once — check WHOOP's current terms before budgeting.

items.title: ExerciseDB becomes AscendAPI, with free V1 and V2 tiers
items.summary: The exercisedb.dev home page now reads "Previously ExerciseDB" above the name AscendAPI, and AscendAPI's documentation (pages last modified in March 2026) describes two products. ExerciseDB V1 has a free hosted tier of "1,500 exercises with 180p GIFs. No authentication required" at oss.exercisedb.dev, plus a paid RapidAPI tier; ExerciseDB V2, on RapidAPI only, gives each exercise an MP4 video and has a free Basic plan of 2,000 requests a month and 200 exercises, on which "free tier media is watermarked". This site first saw the AscendAPI name on 2026-10-22; neither the rename's date nor the paid prices are published on the pages we could read.

items.title: Nutritionix open free tier reportedly curtailed
items.summary: Reports conflict on whether Nutritionix's open free tier still exists; higher tiers route through a Syndigo sales contact. If the free tier is gone, the freemium classification shifts toward sales-gated.

items.title: Oura personal access tokens deprecated
items.summary: Oura deprecated personal access tokens in December 2025 — scripts and internal tools built on PATs need the OAuth flow instead. This page's phrasing has been quoted back to us in search queries, a sign assistants cite it.

items.title: ANT+ membership and certification programs discontinued (reported)
items.summary: Per widely-quoted announcements from the ANT+ organization — the official page was unreachable in our research pass, so this stays reported — the ANT+ membership and certification programs were discontinued on June 30, 2025, with certification applications accepted only until March 31, 2025. Device profiles and documentation reportedly remain available and existing devices are unaffected; coverage cites the EU Radio Equipment Directive as a driver. For new fitness apps, BLE is the practical default radio.
items.sourceLabel: ANT+ vs Bluetooth for fitness sensors

items.title: Strava tightened its developer program
items.summary: Strava tightened developer-program rules in 2024 — the start of the stricter display, branding, and access regime its API operates under today.

items.title: MoveNet: no model updates observed since 2024
items.summary: No updates to the MoveNet pose models have been observed since 2024. The single-person models remain Apache-2.0; treat the weights as stable rather than evolving.

items.title: Google Fit: new developer sign-ups closed
items.summary: Google closed Google Fit API sign-ups for new developers on May 1, 2024 — the first hard milestone of the Fit sunset. Existing integrations continued to work. Google's documentation stated the date when we checked on July 31, 2026; its current Fit migration guide (updated September 10, 2026) no longer repeats it.

items.title: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker weights: last modification
items.summary: The served MediaPipe Pose Landmarker .task model files were last modified in April 2023. The framework evolves; the pose weights have not — pin versions and treat model updates as an event, not a stream.
